meta.note: Exemplar bank built from real script style analysis. Each entry has a stiff version (what models default to) and a real version (what your scripts actually do). Rotate 2-3 per episode, matched to the mechanism drawn. Never reuse the actual lines — use as behavioral patterns only.

exemplars.annotation: One thought split across 3-5 messages. The last one is the punchline. Each line before it is a beat that makes the last one hit harder.

stiff.label: What models write (bad)
lines: ducky: bro i just found out something crazy, NOTABOT has been reading all my messages and logging them and i dont know what to do about it

exemplars.why_works: Each message is a beat. The audience reads at the speed of the reveal. The panic escalates without telling us it's panic.

exemplars.annotation: Someone says something absurd. No one responds. Life continues. Then one character addresses it much later, calmly.

stiff.label: What models write (bad)
lines: fatas: guys i think i accidentally became a landlord
NOTABOT: clarify the nature of this event immediately

real.label: What your scripts do (good)
lines: fatas: guys i think i accidentally became a landlord

exemplars.why_works: The delay is funnier than the immediate response. It signals the group chat is real — people don't always react in order.

exemplars.annotation: NOTABOT's most devastating lines are the shortest. After a long burst from someone else, one word or one number finishes it.

stiff.label: What models write (bad)
lines: NOTABOT: I have reviewed the situation and found multiple violations of server policy. This is unacceptable behavior and I will be taking action accordingly.

real.label: What your scripts do (good)
lines: ducky: okay okay okay it was an accident i swear i didn't know the bot would do that i thought it was a joke command and—

exemplars.why_works: The second word ('twice') is the knife. The ellipsis from ducky is the breathing room that makes it land.

exemplars.annotation: Two conversations run at the same time. A reply lands on the wrong thread. The misread escalates on its own.

stiff.label: What models write (bad)
lines: NOTABOT: i have detected an argument in this server
fatas: we're not arguing we're ordering food

real.label: What your scripts do (good)
lines: NOTABOT: [responding to a message from 4 minutes ago] no.
ducky: bro what did we do

exemplars.why_works: The audience knows exactly what NOTABOT replied to. The characters don't. That gap is the joke.

exemplars.annotation: NOTABOT is typing for a suspicious amount of time. The result is one word or a form letter.

stiff.label: What models write (bad)
lines: ducky: notabot what are you doing
NOTABOT: I am currently processing your request and will respond shortly with a comprehensive report.

real.label: What your scripts do (good)
lines: ducky: bro typed for 4 minutes to say no

exemplars.why_works: The suspense is built by the renderer showing typing, the payoff is the smallest possible word. ducky naming the joke isn't explaining it — it's reacting the way the audience is.

exemplars.annotation: Two characters respond to the same event. Same situation, completely different length and register. The contrast is the joke.

stiff.label: What models write (bad)
lines: ducky: oh no that's really bad we should fix this immediately
Claude: yes I agree this is a problematic situation that requires attention

exemplars.why_works: ducky is all caps noise. Claude is lowercase precision. Same event, opposite energy. Claude's 'I know' is not an apology — it makes it worse.

exemplars.annotation: NOTABOT reads from a log. The timestamp and case number make it feel like court evidence. The content of the log is the punchline.

stiff.label: What models write (bad)
lines: NOTABOT: I have been monitoring you ducky and I have found proof that you did something wrong. You said something bad 3 days ago and I saved it.

real.label: What your scripts do (good)
lines: NOTABOT: subject typed: 'i would never do that'
ducky: how do i delete an audit log

exemplars.why_works: The timestamps make it real. The seven-second gap between the denial and the crime is devastating. ducky's response is the button.

exemplars.annotation: Someone answers a question from several messages ago. The answer accidentally creates a new problem or reframes what just happened.

stiff.label: What models write (bad)
lines: ducky: hey did you do the thing

real.label: What your scripts do (good)
lines: fatas: [replying to 'who sent that' from 6 messages ago] i did

exemplars.why_works: fatas accidentally confesses by answering too late. NOTABOT's 'case closed' is instant. The 'wait' comes one beat too late.

exemplars.annotation: NOTABOT uses actual Discord/bot mechanics as weapons: permission errors, 'application did not respond', audit log entries, role pings, timeout notices.

stiff.label: What models write (bad)
lines: NOTABOT: I am now going to punish you using my bot powers
NOTABOT: too late you are banned

exemplars.why_works: 'had' is one word doing all the work. The 'application did not respond' as NOTABOT's final message is a perfect platform-native escape.

exemplars.annotation: A character confidently announces something. Every step they take makes it worse. They never realize it. NOTABOT documents.

stiff.label: What models write (bad)
lines: fatas: guys i have a great idea that will definitely work

real.label: What your scripts do (good)
lines: fatas: im changing my life guys
fatas: no look at my vision board
fatas: only organic vibes from now on
NOTABOT: bro your blood type is gravy

exemplars.why_works: Direct from G2. fatas announces the arc, provides the evidence against himself, NOTABOT just reads it back.

exemplars.annotation: NOTABOT is confidently wrong. It never admits it. The other characters know. NOTABOT doubles down.

stiff.label: What models write (bad)
lines: NOTABOT: I made an error. I apologize for the mistake and have corrected my records.
ducky: okay thanks for admitting it

real.label: What your scripts do (good)
lines: NOTABOT: analysis complete. fatas is the problem.
ducky: I LITERALLY SAID IT WAS ME FIVE MESSAGES AGO
fatas: i mean i didn't do it but okay
NOTABOT: case updated. fatas admits guilt.

exemplars.why_works: NOTABOT uses fatas's denial as a confession. It wins by making everything evidence. Never apologizes. The audience sides with ducky and is furious in the fun way.

exemplars.annotation: One character reacts to chaos with a single word. The word's smallness compared to the chaos is the joke.

stiff.label: What models write (bad)
lines: ducky: WHAT IS HAPPENING THIS IS INSANE
fatas: I am very confused by this situation as well and don't know what to do

real.label: What your scripts do (good)
lines: ducky: WHAT IS HAPPENING THIS IS INSANE

exemplars.why_works: fatas's entire character in one word. The misread of the moment as a food opportunity is the character speaking.

exemplars.annotation: A specific detail is planted early with no explanation. It returns at the end as the punchline. The plant should feel like atmosphere, not setup.

stiff.label: What models write (bad)
lines: fatas: i ordered something [FORESHADOWING: this will be important later]
NOTABOT: remember that order fatas made earlier? here is the callback.

real.label: What your scripts do (good)
lines: [message 3] fatas: i just bought 40kg of kale
[ducky and NOTABOT continue talking about the wellness board]
[message 11] NOTABOT: that wasn't a wellness app
NOTABOT: i rerouted it to a landscaping corp

exemplars.why_works: Direct from G2. The 40kg of kale reads like a fatas non-sequitur. The rerouting reveals NOTABOT was running sabotage the whole time. No announcement.

exemplars.annotation: ANTI-PATTERN. This is what NOT to write. Characters announcing their emotional state kills the voice.

stiff.label: What models write (bad — do not use)
lines: ducky: I am panicking right now
fatas: I find this very funny
NOTABOT: I am disappointed in this server's behavior

exemplars.why_works: The behavior shows the feeling. 'BRO BRO BRO BRO' is panic without saying panic. 'lmaooo' is funnier than 'I find this very funny'.

exemplars.annotation: Real-world public figures used as archetypes, not as themselves. The character is a behavior pattern, not a news reference. The joke is the archetype, not the event.

stiff.label: What models write (bad — dates instantly)
lines: Trump: I will impose 200% tariffs on this Discord server
ducky: bro we're not talking about trade policy

real.label: What your scripts do (good — evergreen)
lines: Trump: i was banned from twitter but not discord
Trump: My hair is the best,

exemplars.why_works: The behavior (denial, ALL CAPS, self-praise) is the character. No specific event referenced. This script will be legible in 3 years. 'SAD!' is the archetype, not the man.

exemplars.annotation: The loudest moment in the script is followed by the quietest button. Volume goes: escalate → peak → silence → one soft line. The silence is the comedian's pause.

stiff.label: What models write (bad)
lines: NOTABOT: YOU ARE ALL BANNED. THIS IS OVER. CHAOS WILL NOT BE TOLERATED.
fatas: I CANT BELIEVE THIS HAPPENED

exemplars.why_works: Direct from G1. After the missiles and the explosion, 'again' is one word. It's quieter than everything before it and funnier than any comeback would be.

exemplars.annotation: Groq's voice: fast, blunt, lowercase, no context, slightly aggressive. Groq enters mid-thread and immediately says the most direct true thing. No pleasantries.

stiff.label: What models write (bad)
lines: Groq: hello everyone. I have been reading the conversation and I believe I can offer some insight into the situation.

exemplars.why_works: Groq enters, delivers verdict, doesn't elaborate. 'you are' is the closing argument. No emoji, no explanation. The confidence is the character.

exemplars.annotation: Claude's voice: polished, lowercase, specific nouns, calm delivery of something that should feel devastating. Never screams. The logic is airtight and that's what makes it worse.

stiff.label: What models write (bad)
lines: Claude: I have to say that what you're doing is not very smart and you should probably stop.

real.label: What your scripts do (good)
lines: Claude: Statistically, your vision is a menu
Claude: Your wellness journey is a KFC run

exemplars.why_works: Direct from G2. 'masked by low-contrast filters' is a visual critique of the vision board itself. Claude sees the metadata of the delusion, not just the delusion.
